dependencies.reason: Delivers the PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE workspace variable this spec reads to decide whether to attempt the single-branch fetch, and establishes the origin-remote credential and go-git fetch conventions (workspace.ResolveCloneAuth, the fetch call shape verified against internal/upstream, treating git.NoErrAlreadyUpToDate as success) that this spec's single-branch fetch reuses rather than re-deriving.

tasks.title: Implement the three-step branch resolution engine (local, origin tracking, origin fetch)
steps: In internal/workspace/branch_check_hook.go, add a BranchResolution string type with constants BranchResolutionLocal, BranchResolutionOriginTracking, BranchResolutionOriginFetch, and an ErrCredentialResolutionFailed sentinel error; change BranchCheckFunc to func(slug, branchName string, attemptMutation bool) (BranchResolution, error), documenting that attemptMutation=false must perform only the read-only refs/heads/<name> check (no ref write, no fetch, no wslock call), and attemptMutation=true means the caller already holds the workspace's wslock for the duration of the call, so the hook performs ref writes/fetch but must never call wslock itself

In internal/carrypatch, add branch_resolution.go defining BranchResolutionConfig{WorkspaceRoot string, NewGitRunner func(repoPath string) (GitRunner, error), GetVariable GetVariableFunc, ResolveOriginAuth func(slug string) (transport.AuthMethod, error)} and NewBranchResolutionHook(cfg BranchResolutionConfig) workspace.BranchCheckFunc

Implement step (a): rev-parse --verify refs/heads/<name> via the GitRunner; return workspace.BranchResolutionLocal on success; when attemptMutation is false and this fails, return a distinct not-found error without doing anything else

Implement step (b), reached only when attemptMutation is true: rev-parse --verify refs/remotes/origin/<name>; on success run update-ref refs/heads/<name> <sha> and return workspace.BranchResolutionOriginTracking

Read PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE via cfg.GetVariable("workspace", slug, "PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE") fresh on every call (never cached); treat an empty value, a read error, or any value other than "origin" as hub, returning the not-found error without fetching

Implement step (c): resolve fork credentials via cfg.ResolveOriginAuth(slug); wrap a non-nil error as fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", workspace.ErrCredentialResolutionFailed, err); otherwise perform a go-git single-branch fetch of +refs/heads/<name>:refs/remotes/origin/<name> against the "origin" remote (git.PlainOpen + repo.Remote("origin") + FetchContext with git.NoTags, matching internal/upstream.Fetch's call shape and treating errors.Is(err, git.NoErrAlreadyUpToDate) as success); any other fetch error folds into the not-found error (Design Decision 5); on success re-check the tracking ref and, if present, update-ref + return workspace.BranchResolutionOriginFetch

Write TS-03-1 through TS-03-6 as white-box tests in internal/carrypatch against real temporary git repositories built with the runGitCmd/setupCarryPatchRepo-style helpers already in internal/carrypatch/testhelpers_test.go, using a stub GetVariable and a second temp repo added as the "origin" remote for the fetch case; confirm they fail before the implementation and pass after

Write TS-03-25 (no fork credentials configured resolves to nil auth and the fetch still proceeds) and TS-03-26 (a non-credential fetch failure, e.g. the requested branch absent on the fake origin, folds into the same not-found error rather than being classified as a credential failure)
Run go test ./internal/carrypatch/... and go vet ./... and fix any issues

tasks.title: Wire single-patch registration to the resolution engine with lock orchestration, 400/409/502 mapping and audit metadata
steps: In internal/workspace, add a resolveBranches(slug string, items []branchResolveItem) helper (branchResolveItem{branchName string; skip bool}) plus an injectable package var wsLockTryLock = wslock.TryLock for testability: for each item in submitted order, when item.skip or branchCheckHook==nil resolve to "" (no attempt, no lock, no read/write); otherwise call branchCheckHook(slug, branchName, false); on success record the resolution and continue; on failure, lazily call wsLockTryLock(slug) at most once for the whole resolveBranches call (reusing an already-acquired lock for later items), returning a workspace-busy result immediately if it fails; while holding the lock, call branchCheckHook(slug, branchName, true) and record its resolution or propagate its error; release the lock (if acquired) before returning, and report the index of the first failing item (-1 if none)

In handleAddPatchSingle, replace the direct branchCheckHook(slug, branchName) call with resolveBranches(slug, a one-item slice); map its outcome to: workspace-busy -> HTTP 409 with error_type "workspace_busy" (reuse the "another operation is running on this workspace; retry later" message already used by sync/reclone/rebuild); workspace.ErrCredentialResolutionFailed -> HTTP 502 "credential resolution failed"; any other error -> HTTP 400 "branch does not exist in repository or on origin" (replacing the old "branch does not exist in repository" text)
Include the resolved BranchResolution in the hub.patch.create metadata map under "branch_resolution", omitted when the resolution is "" (skip_branch_check bypass or no hook registered)

Update cmd/af-hub/main.go's workspace.RegisterBranchCheckHook call to register carrypatch.NewBranchResolutionHook(carrypatch.BranchResolutionConfig{WorkspaceRoot: cfg.Workspace.Path, NewGitRunner: cpGitRunnerFactory, GetVariable: store.GetVariableValue, ResolveOriginAuth: func(slug string) (transport.AuthMethod, error) { return workspace.ResolveCloneAuth(store, slug) }}), removing the old one-line rev-parse closure

Update internal/workspace/carry_patch_patches_test.go's existing RegisterBranchCheckHook(...) stub closures to the new three-argument, two-return signature so the package keeps compiling, preserving each stub's existing pass/fail intent

Write TS-03-7 (400 not-found, single request), TS-03-9 (skip_branch_check bypass leaves the hook uncalled, single), TS-03-11 (wslock acquired before the update-ref/fetch of a mutating resolution) and TS-03-14 (no wslock call for the already-local fast path)
Write TS-03-12 (lock already held by another operation -> 409 workspace_busy, no ref or row written) and TS-03-13 (lock released before addPatchWithPosition runs; the request still succeeds)

Write TS-03-19 (audit metadata carries branch_resolution), TS-03-21 (skip_branch_check omits branch_resolution) and TS-03-22 (property: recorded branch_resolution always equals the actual resolving placement across local/origin_tracking/origin_fetch)
Write TS-03-23 (single-request credential-resolution failure aborts with 502 "credential resolution failed", writing no ref and no row)
Run go test ./internal/workspace/... ./cmd/... and go vet ./... and fix any issues

tasks.title: Wire batch patch registration to the shared-lock resolution and per-patch audit emission
steps: In handleAddPatchBatch, remove the per-element branchCheckHook call from the existing syntactic-validation loop (branch_name required, valid ref, not-integration-branch, position >= 1 stay unchanged) and, after that loop, call resolveBranches(slug, items) once for the whole submitted array (one item per element, carrying each element's skip_branch_check), before the duplicate-name-in-batch and already-registered-in-db checks

Map a resolveBranches failure to the batch's existing "patch[<i>]: ..." response shape: workspace-busy -> 409 workspace_busy; workspace.ErrCredentialResolutionFailed -> 502 "patch[<i>]: credential resolution failed"; any other error -> 400 "patch[<i>]: branch does not exist in repository or on origin" (replacing the old text), where <i> is the returned failIndex

After the existing atomic addPatchesBatch insert succeeds, emit one hub.patch.create audit event per inserted patch, in insertion order, each carrying branch_name, position, and branch_resolution (omitted when that element's resolution is "")
Write TS-03-8 (batch 400 naming the failing index, no row inserted) and TS-03-16 (stops at the first failing element; later elements are never resolved)
Write TS-03-15 (exactly one wslock acquisition for a batch mixing local, origin_tracking, and origin_fetch elements) and TS-03-18 (lock released before the atomic insert when every element resolves)
Write TS-03-17 (a local branch created for an earlier successful element stays in place after a later element fails the batch)
Write TS-03-20 (one hub.patch.create event per inserted patch, each with its own branch_resolution) and TS-03-24 (batch credential-resolution failure aborts with 502 naming the failing index)
Write TS-03-10 (property: skip_branch_check=true never invokes the hook and never records branch_resolution, checked across both PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE modes and both single and batch request shapes)
Run go test ./internal/workspace/... and go vet ./... and fix any issues

Add patches" step: remove the sentence stating branches are "validated against the workspace repository at add time" and replace it with one or two sentences describing tracking-ref promotion and, in origin mode, the single-branch fetch fallback, without restructuring the surrounding Getting Started walkthrough (that restructuring is patch_divergence_recovery's work)

Write TS-03-27, TS-03-28 and TS-03-29 as content-assertion tests reusing the existing readDocFile/projectRoot helpers in internal/workspace/docs_spec03_test.go, confirming they fail before the doc edits and pass after

tasks.title: Verify the fork-branch registration paths end to end against real git repositories
steps: Write TS-03-30 as a real-component test: wire workspace.RegisterBranchCheckHook(carrypatch.NewBranchResolutionHook(...)) exactly as cmd/af-hub/main.go does, against a real temporary trunk git repository whose "origin" remote already carries the branch as a tracking ref, and confirm afc-equivalent POST /workspaces/:slug/patches creates refs/heads/<name> and records branch_resolution=origin_tracking

Write TS-03-31 against a real local "fork" remote (a second temp git repository added as the origin remote) reachable for a real go-git fetch, with the workspace's PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE variable resolving to origin, confirming refs/remotes/origin/<name> and refs/heads/<name> are created and branch_resolution=origin_fetch is recorded

Write TS-03-32: a batch of three elements where the first attempt fails at index 2, confirming the local branch created for element 1 is left in place, then a corrected retry inserts all three rows and emits three hub.patch.create events each with its own branch_resolution

Write TS-03-33: a goroutine or a directly-held wslock.TryLock(slug) simulates a concurrent sync; confirm registration returns 409 workspace_busy while it is held and succeeds with resolution origin_tracking once released

Trace 03-PATH-1 through 03-PATH-4 against the real code: confirm handleAddPatchSingle/handleAddPatchBatch call branchCheckHook exactly as registered in cmd/af-hub/main.go, that resolveBranches acquires wsLockTryLock before any mutating hook call and releases it before addPatchWithPosition/addPatchesBatch runs, and that carrypatch.NewBranchResolutionHook's fetch step is reached only in PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin mode

For every criterion carrying a contract in 03-REQ-1, 03-REQ-2, 03-REQ-4, 03-REQ-5, 03-REQ-6 and 03-REQ-7, confirm the producing value (BranchResolution, or the not-found/workspace-busy/credential-resolution-failed outcomes) is consumed by handleAddPatchSingle/handleAddPatchBatch in production code (HTTP status, error body, audit metadata), not only by a test double
Grep internal/workspace, internal/carrypatch and cmd/af-hub for TODO and panic("not implemented") introduced while building this spec and confirm none remain
Confirm cmd/af-hub/main.go's RegisterBranchCheckHook call is the sole production wiring point (no leftover one-line rev-parse closure) and is reachable from server startup
Run make test and make lint and confirm both pass
done_when: go test ./... -count=1 passes with TS-03-30 through TS-03-33 exercising real git repositories, a real wslock, and a real audit emitter rather than test doubles
